text.brief: In July 1936 Edgar Snow sat with Mao Zedong in a cave at Bao'an and wrote down the life story that Mao chose to tell him.
text.record: The Party arranged Snow's passage into its base in the summer of 1936, and he stayed about four months ([Edgar Snow, Interviews With Mao Tse-tung (his own account, via marxists.org)](https://www.marxists.org/reference/archive/mao/works/1936/11/x01.htm); [Season of High Adventure: Edgar Snow in China (UC Press; secondary)](https://publishing.cdlib.org/ucpressebooks/public/book/season-of-high-adventure-edgar-snow-in-china.html)). Red Star Over China appeared in London in 1937 and in New York in January 1938, and a Chinese translation drew young volunteers to Yan'an (["Who is CPC?": Edgar Snow, the first Western journalist to introduce Red China to the world (PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 2022)](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/zy/jj/zggcddwjw100ggs/gmqtjygml/202406/t20240606_11377907.html)). The book set the Western picture of the Party for a decade.
text.reading: One curated visit wrote the adversary's first Western profile, and the host chose every interview. The Party still grants access to the visitors it expects to carry its picture home.
text.gapText: Data Architecture. The defenders held one source on the Party's base and no means to test it.
text.fix: Treat any access an adversary grants as a curated feed, and test it against sources the adversary does not control.
